Good — here’s a focused 1-week deload that keeps the same exercises your client has been using but reduces volume and intensity so they recover without losing movement practice. Plan assumes 3 full-body sessions/week (standard after a 4‑week hypertrophy block) — if your client trained more frequently during the previous block, you can distribute these sessions across the same number of days but keep the same relative reductions.

Deload goals
- Reduce training volume to ~35–50% of the previous working set total.
- Reduce intensity to RPE 6–7 on compounds (no sets to failure).
- Keep the same movement patterns and exercises to maintain motor patterns.
- Preserve accessory movement but with lighter loads and fewer sets.
- Focus on recovery: sleep, nutrition at maintenance to slight surplus, mobility, soft tissue, and low-load aerobic work.

How to interpret sets/weights
- If they were doing 18 working sets per session at RPE ~8.5, drop to ~6–8 working sets per session total (approximately 35–45%).
- Use ~60–70% of habitual working weights for compound lifts, or use the same weights but drop to RPE 6–7 (stop 3–4 reps short of failure).
- Keep tempo controlled, full ROM, focus on technique and breathing.

One-week deload plan (3 sessions, full gym). Warm-up before every session: 8–12 minutes total (5–8 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility for the main joints + 2 lighter warm-up sets of the first compound if needed).

Session A — Squat focus
1) Back squat — 3 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 6–7 (use ~60–70% of normal working weight)
2) Romanian deadlift (RDL) — 2 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 6
3) Leg press or front squat (if previously used front squat) — 1 set x 8 reps @ RPE 6–7 (keep it light)
4) Walking lunges (dumbbells) — 2 sets x 8 steps per leg (slow, controlled)
5) Calf raise (standing or seated) — 2 sets x 10–12 reps @ easy-moderate
6) Core: Plank variations — 2 x 45–60 sec OR Pallof press 2 x 8–10 each side (light)

Notes: Rest 90–150s between compound sets; 60–90s for accessories. Maintain clean technique; no explosive max efforts.

Session B — Press/pull (upper-body) focus
1) Bench press (or incline bench if that’s the usual press) — 3 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 6–7 (~60–70% usual)
2) Bent-over row or chest-supported row (whichever you used previously) — 2 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 6
3) Overhead press (if previously included) — 1–2 sets x 5–6 reps @ RPE 6 (keep light)
4) Pull-ups or lat pull-down — 2 sets x 6–8 reps (assisted if needed to keep RPE 6–7)
5) Lateral raises — 2 sets x 10–12 reps @ easy
6) Biceps or triceps accessory (your usual preference) — 2 sets x 8–10 reps (light)
7) Core: Dead bug 2 sets x 10–12 per side

Notes: Rest 90–150s for main lifts, 60s for accessories. Emphasize scapular control and thoracic mobility.

Session C — Deadlift/hinge & posterior chain emphasis
1) Conventional or trap-bar deadlift — 3 sets x 3–5 reps @ RPE 6–7 (use ~60–70% usual; if heavy neurologically, do 3 sets of 3)
2) Barbell hip thrust — 2 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 6
3) Good morning or back extension (light) — 1–2 sets x 8–10 reps
4) Single-leg RDL or Bulgarian split squat — 2 sets x 6–8 reps per leg (light)

6) Core: Farmer carry 2 x 40–60 m (light load)

Notes: Deadlift intensity is reduced — avoid heavy singles. Keep tempo controlled and stop well short of failure.

Optional light conditioning (1–2 low-intensity sessions across the week)
- 20–30 minutes easy bike, brisk walk, or easy row (conversational pace)
- Include mobility and 10–15 minutes of targeted soft-tissue work (foam roll, lacrosse ball) and stretching after one of these sessions.

- Protein: Maintain ~1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight (for a 26-year-old male advanced lifter, stay at upper end of range; e.g., 1.8–2.0 g/kg).
- Carbohydrate: Moderate to support training sessions; front-load carbs around training days.
- Sleep: Prioritize 7.5–9 hours/night.
- Active recovery: Light aerobic sessions, mobility, and daily steps (6–10k) to encourage circulation.
- Hydration: Maintain consistent hydration; include electrolytes if heavy sweat.

- Keep about 3–4+ reps in reserve on the main sets.
- If the client feels unusually fatigued, reduce session count to 2 and keep the same set structure.

Here is the complete 1‑week deload with every adjustment rolled in: reduced overall volume, bench substituted for a shoulder‑friendly chest movement, a 20‑minute mobility session, two 30‑minute Zone‑2 cardio sessions, allowance to push Wednesday and Friday (but still controlled), and guidance for low‑fatigue strength markers. Use this as the document you hand to the client.

Weekly summary
- Baseline: ~18 working sets/session in prior hypertrophy block
- Deload target: overall weekly reduction; per session targets adjusted across the week:
  - Monday (true deload): 6 working sets
  - Wednesday (elevated): 9 working sets
  - Friday (elevated): 9 working sets
  - Weekly total = 24 working sets (well below previous weekly total ~54)
- Intensity caps:
  - True deload sets: RPE 6–7
  - Elevated day main sets: up to RPE 8 (stop ~2 RIR)
  - Accessories: RPE ≤ 7 (prefer RPE 5–6)
  - No maximal singles, no chasing failure
- Warm-ups: 8–12 minutes before every gym session (5–8 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility + 2 light ramp warm-up sets of the first compound). Warm-up sets do not count toward working-set totals.
- Mobility session: Thursday, 20 minutes (light).
- Zone‑2 cardio: Tuesday and Saturday, 30 minutes each (conversational pace).
- Strength markers: allowed once on a pushed day (replace one working set), submaximal only — see notes below.

Schedule (example)
- Monday: Session A — Squat focus (true deload) — 6 working sets
- Tuesday: Zone‑2 cardio 30 min
- Wednesday: Session B — Upper (incline DB press substitute) — elevated — 9 working sets + optional single test set substitution
- Thursday: Mobility 20 min
- Friday: Session C — Deadlift/posterior chain — elevated — 9 working sets + optional single test set substitution
- Saturday: Zone‑2 cardio 30 min or easy active recovery
- Sunday: Rest

Detailed session plans

Monday — Session A (True deload) — Total working sets = 6
Goal: recovery, movement quality, low fatigue
Warm-up: 8–12 min (5–8 min easy bike/row + dynamic hip/knee/ankle mobility + 2 light warm-up sets of squat)

Working sets
1) Back squat — 2 x 5 @ RPE 6 (leave ~4 RIR) — 2 sets
2) Romanian deadlift (RDL) — 1 x 6–8 @ RPE 6 — 1 set
3) Walking lunges (dumbbells) — 1 x 8 steps per leg — 1 set
4) Standing or seated calf raise — 1 x 10–12 — 1 set
5) Core: Plank or Pallof press — 1 x 45–60 sec OR 1 x 8–10 each side (counts as 1 set)
Totals: 6 working sets (note: depending on how you count core, the practical working-set count for session goals is met)

Rest: 90–150s between compound sets, 60–90s accessories
Notes: Keep tempo controlled, full ROM, and stop well short of failure.

Tuesday — Zone‑2 Cardio
- 30 minutes easy bike/row/brisk walk or light jog
- Intensity: conversational pace (~60–70% max HR, RPE 3–4/10)
- Purpose: maintain aerobic base, promote recovery.

Wednesday — Session B (Elevated upper) — Total working sets = 9
Goal: increase engagement; heavier but controlled. Cap main sets at RPE 8. Optionally place a submax strength marker here by replacing one working set (see testing guidance).

Warm-up: 8–12 min (cardio + banded shoulder prep + 2 light incline DB warm-up sets)

Working sets
1) Incline dumbbell press (15–30°, neutral/slightly rotated grip) — 4 x 5 @ RPE 7–8 — 4 sets
   - Alternative if shoulder reacts: Floor press 4 x 5 @ RPE 7–8 or machine chest press 4 x 6–8.
2) Bent-over row or chest‑supported row — 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 7 — 2 sets
3) Overhead press — 1 x 5–6 @ RPE 7–8 — 1 set
   - If overhead not tolerated: replace with 1 x 6–8 banded face pulls + 1 x 12 banded external rotations (count together as 1 working set)
4) Pull-up or lat pulldown — 1 x 6–8 @ RPE 7 — 1 set
5) Lateral raises or light face pulls (scapular health) — 1 x 10–12 — 1 set
Totals: 9 working sets

Rest: 2–3 minutes for heavier sets (incline/overhead), 60–90s for accessories

Wednesday testing option (if tracking a marker)
- Replace one of the incline DB working sets (preferably the last set) with a single submax test set:
  - Example: 1 x 6 at a prechosen weight to RPE 8 (stop ~2 RIR). Record load, reps, RPE.
  - Count this as one working set.
- Do NOT perform multiple attempts or chase heavier loads.

Thursday — Mobility Session — 20 minutes (light)
Goal: thoracic extension, shoulder ROM, hip mobility, breathing. Pain‑free only.

Structure (20 min)
1) 2–3 min diaphragmatic breathing (supine/seated) — slow controlled breaths
2) Thoracic mobility (5 min)
   - Foam‑roller thoracic extensions: 2 x 8–10 slow reps
   - Thread‑the‑needle or quadruped rotations: 2 x 8 per side
3) Shoulder mobility (5 min)
   - Banded pull‑aparts + external rotation combo: 2 x 10–12
   - Wall slides or small‑range dislocates: 2 x 8–10
   - Scapular retraction holds: 3 x 8–10 sec
4) Hip/hamstring mobility (5 min)
   - Couch stretch or 90/90 hip opener: 2 x 30–45s per side
   - Hip CARs or controlled leg swings: 1 x 6–8 per side
5) Finish: 1–2 min light soft‑tissue self‑massage or banded pulls

Notes: Keep all positions pain‑free; slow reps and emphasis on breathing.

Friday — Session C (Elevated posterior chain) — Total working sets = 9
Goal: more intensity for posterior chain while keeping RPE ≤ 8 and avoiding maximal singles.

Warm-up: 8–12 min (bike + hip/hamstring mobility + 2 ramp warm-up sets for deadlift)

Working sets
1) Deadlift (trap bar preferred for lower CNS cost, or conventional) — 4 x 3–4 @ RPE 7–8 — 4 sets
   - If trap bar used, this is less stressful; choose 3–4 reps per set.
2) Barbell hip thrust — 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 7 — 2 sets
3) Single‑leg RDL or Bulgarian split squat — 1 x 6–8 per leg — 1 set
4) Hamstring curl (machine) — 1 x 10–12 — 1 set
Totals: 9 working sets

Rest: 2–3 minutes on deadlift sets; 60–90s on accessories

Friday testing option (if tracking a marker)
- Replace one deadlift working set with a submax test set (1 x 3–4 at RPE 8) and record load/reps/RPE. Count as one working set. No multiple attempts.

Saturday — Zone‑2 Cardio (30 min)
- 30 minutes easy bike/row/brisk walk
- Intensity: conversational (Zone 2 — RPE 3–4/10)
- Optional: short mobility warm-up and light walking after session.

Sunday — Rest
- Full rest. Monitor soreness, sleep, and energy. If unusually sore or fatigued, consider an extra rest day.

Strength‑marker testing guidance (low fatigue)
- Only one test set per pushed session (Wednesday or Friday), replace a planned working set with the test set.
- Tests must be submaximal: stop at RPE 8 (≈2 RIR). Do NOT chase multiple attempts or 1RM singles.
- Suggested low‑fatigue tests:
  - Lower: Trap‑bar deadlift — 1 x 4 @ submax weight (RPE 8) OR 1 x 3–4 at ~75–80% 1RM (stop at RPE 8).
  - Upper: Incline dumbbell press — 1 x 6 at selected weight (RPE 7–8).
  - Velocity check (if you have a device): 1 x 2 @ 50–60% 1RM on squat — record mean/peak velocity.
- What to record: exercise, load (kg/lb), reps, RPE, and short notes on joint comfort and perceived fatigue. Optional: bar speed values if using a device.
- Safety rule: any sharp joint pain → stop test immediately and substitute with isometric hold or machine variant.

Volume & intensity bookkeeping reminders
- Warm-up sets are not counted in the working set totals.
- Working sets this week = 24 total across three sessions.
- Keep RPE targets: Monday RPE 6–7; Wed/Fri main sets up to RPE 8; accessories ≤ 7.
- If overall fatigue increases, revert Friday to the true deload template or reduce pushed session sets by 1.

Nutrition & recovery (brief)
- Calories: maintenance or +100–200 kcal to assist recovery given the slightly elevated midweek load.
- Protein: ~1.8–2.0 g/kg bodyweight.
- Carbohydrates: target moderate intake, slightly higher around Wed & Fri sessions.
- Sleep: aim 7.5–9 hours nightly.
- Hydration & electrolytes as required.
- Soft tissue/mobility: include 10–15 minutes of soft tissue work after one pushed session if needed.

Coaching cues & contingencies
- Emphasize technique: stop sets on form breakdown rather than chasing reps.
- Monitor shoulder: incline dumbbell press uses neutral grip; if irritation occurs switch to floor press or machine press and add banded external rotations.
- Communication: have client rate session difficulty immediately after sessions and Soreness/Energy 24–48 hours after pushed days. If soreness/energy indicate inadequate recovery, reduce Friday volume or lower Wednesday intensity next session.
- If the client wants exact load targets and warm-up ladders (kg/lb) for the inclined DB press, back squat, and trap‑bar deadlift based on his recent working weights or 1RMs, provide those numbers and I’ll convert RPE targets into exact loads and a two‑set warm‑up ladder per compound.

Deliverable summary (what to hand the client)
- The day-by-day plan above (Monday–Sunday).
- Simple checklist per session: warm-up, exercises with set × reps and RPE cap, rest guidelines, and one line for the test set if planned.
- Mobility and cardio sessions scheduled midweek and weekend.
- Clear instructions on RPE, pain stop rules, and how to record strength markers.

If you want, I can now:
- Convert RPE targets into exact kg targets and a warm-up ladder if you give his recent working weights or 1RMs, or
- Produce a printable one‑page handout for the client with the exercises and the testing protocol.
